messages:
maureen: heads up - RC for py-sdk dropped a subtle init-order regression. If you pass default_route before api_key (e.g., Client(default_route=..., api_key=...)) the route header is not emitted and console shows route_meta=null. Repro below.

devon: ouch. paste repro?

maureen:```python
from redwood import Client
# old (working)
c = Client(api_key='sk_xxx', default_route='acct-42')
c.generate('hello')
# rc (broken)
c = Client(default_route='acct-42', api_key='sk_xxx')
c.generate('hello')
# server sees no x-route header
```

anya: sounds like a race in __init__ where we normalize kwargs before setting self._api_key. Might be from the kwargs-normalize patch.

kevin: confirmed via quick bisect: commit d4f3a2bf introduced normalize_kwargs() call early which accesses route parsing; the api key isn't set on the instance yet.

devon: options: revert the RC change and ship a 0.9.1 patch, or add server-side tolerant parsing (accept legacy query param) while we patch SDK. Thoughts?

maureen: revert+patch is safest for hosted customers. For Dedicated/private we can enable server-side tolerant mapping for a 72h window to reduce impact. Also need telemetry flags so console dashboards can filter affected requests (sdk_version + missing route).

kevin: agree. marking this as a breaking-change candidate if we don't revert; we don't want to bump major during RC. I'll handle the revert PR.

anya: UX ask: can the console surface a small "route missing" panel and an SDK-version heatmap so we can see which versions caused it during the rollout? That would help SRE & CS triage.

oliver: I can spin up an ad-hoc dashboard tile: filter where route_meta is null, group by sdk.name and sdk.version, show last 1h. Will also add an alert if affected share > 0.5% for 5m. Tagging maureen when live.

maureen: opened PR https://git.internal/redwood/py-sdk/pull/4291 reverting the normalize change and adding a unit test for init-order header emission. Also added an integration test hitting a mock proxy to assert headers.

deploy-bot: Canary queued: py-sdk-hosted v0.9.1-canary -> willary group. Logs: canary started.

devon: we should also run a quota-recon run because missing route leads to tenant misattribution; some customers may see usage misbilled. Kevin, can you schedule a small reconciliation job for the last 3h window?

kevin: scheduled a low-priority job; will post results in ~30m. If we find discrepancies we'll backfill console metrics and issue a cs advisory.

maureen: pinging @lina for release notes and Dedicated advisory.

lina: noted - crafting a short advisory for Dedicated + hosted changelog entry. Will include migration guidance: upgrade py-sdk to 0.9.1+, avoid relying on kwarg ordering, and interim server fallback window.

anya: follow-up item: add an SDK lint rule in CI to catch any pattern that references normalized kwargs before required auth fields are set. Might prevent similar regressions.

kevin: good call. I'll add a lint/CI test and include it in the revert PR.

maureen: thanks team. keeping this thread open until canary + quota recon are green.
